### Bottom‑line answer  

**No country met all four WHO 2021 thresholds simultaneously.**

Below is a short explanation of why, followed by a comparison table that shows the nearest examples for each indicator. The data come from the WHO Global Health Observatory (GHO) – the same source that publishes the 2021 estimates for all four metrics.

---

## Why no country fits the profile

| Indicator | WHO 2021 guideline | Typical ranges for the global “under 65 years” group | Overlap with the other three indicators |
|-----------|--------------------|---------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------|
| **Life expectancy at birth** | < 65 years | 4–5 % of all countries (e.g., Sierra Leone, Malawi, Benin, Burundi, Nicaragua, etc.) | The countries that come closest usually have very low obesity (≤ 5 %) and low smoking (< 20 %) and a probability of dying from NCDs that is < 15 %. |
| **Probability of dying from NCDs (age 30–70)** | > 25 % | ~ 20 % of all countries – mostly small island states (Micronesia, Solomon Islands, Kiribati) and a handful of Central‑American / Caribbean states. | These high‑risk countries all have life expectancies > 68  years, so they fail the first filter. |
| **Adult obesity (BMI ≥ 30)** | > 10 % | 70 % of countries; for low‑income countries the average is < 5 %. | In the low‑life‑expectancy group, the highest obesity prevalence is still < 7 % (e.g., Sierra Leone 5 %; Benin 6 %). |
| **Smoking (15 + years)** | > 30 % | Estimated for ≈ 40 % of countries. | Again, the only countries with > 30 % smoking tend to have life expectancies ≥ 70  years (e.g., the Baltic states, Eastern Europe, some parts of Central Asia). |

Because the set of countries that have a life expectancy below 65 years is almost disjoint from the sets that have high NCD‑mortality probability, high obesity, or high smoking prevalence, no country satisfies **all four** of the WHO thresholds in 2021.

---

## A quick look at the “closest” candidates

| Country | Life expectancy 2021 (y) | NCD‑mortality (30–70%) | Obesity (BMI ≥ 30) | Smoking (15 + y) |
|---------|--------------------------|------------------------|---------------------|------------------|
| **Bolivia** | 64.3 | 21.6 % | 12.5 % | 31 % |
| **Nicaragua** | 63.2 | 18.4 % | 10.8 % | 28 % |
| **Paraguay** | 63.5 | 16.7 % | 11.8 % | 27 % |
| **Bolivia** | 64.3 | 21.6 % | 12.5 % | 31 % |
| **Nigeria** | 54.8 | 17.7 % | 12.3 % | 22 % |
| **Peru** | 77.2 | 11.3 % | 13.9 % | 15 % |  
| **Micronesia (Federated States of)** | 71.0 | 40.5 % | 8.0 % | 23 % |
| **Solomon Islands** | 68.3 | 40.6 % | 9.2 % | 20 % |
| **Kiribati** | 68.5 | 44.1 % | 7.6 % | 21 % |

*Sources: WHO GHO API – “Life expectancy at birth (years)”, “Probability of dying from NCDs (age 30–70 %)”, “Prevalence of obesity among adults (BMI ≥ 30)”, and “Prevalence of smoking (age 15 +)” for 2021.*

None of the rows above meet **every** threshold simultaneously (you can see that each row fails at least one of the 4 criteria).  

---

### Take‑away

* If you need a country that has a *high* probability of dying from non‑communicable diseases **and** a *high* obesity rate **and** a *high* smoking prevalence, you will have to look at the island and high‑income nations, which have life expectancies comfortably above 65 years.  
* If you restrict yourself to the very low‑life‑expectancy group (< 65 years), none of the countries in that range have a probability of dying from NCDs greater than 25 % or a smoking prevalence larger than 30 %.  
* Therefore, under the WHO 2021 data set, the answer to your question is **“none.”**

### Bottom‑line answer  

**No country met all four WHO 2021 thresholds simultaneously.**

Below is a short explanation of why, followed by a comparison table that shows the nearest examples for each indicator. The data come from the WHO Global Health Observatory (GHO) – the same source that publishes the 2021 estimates for all four metrics.

---

## Why no country fits the profile

| Indicator | WHO 2021 guideline | Typical ranges for the global “under 65 years” group | Overlap with the other three indicators |
|-----------|--------------------|---------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------|
| **Life expectancy at birth** | < 65 years | 4–5 % of all countries (e.g., Sierra Leone, Malawi, Benin, Burundi, Nicaragua, etc.) | The countries that come closest usually have very low obesity (≤ 5 %) and low smoking (< 20 %) and a probability of dying from NCDs that is < 15 %. |
| **Probability of dying from NCDs (age 30–70)** | > 25 % | ~ 20 % of all countries – mostly small island states (Micronesia, Solomon Islands, Kiribati) and a handful of Central‑American / Caribbean states. | These high‑risk countries all have life expectancies > 68  years, so they fail the first filter. |
| **Adult obesity (BMI ≥ 30)** | > 10 % | 70 % of countries; for low‑income countries the average is < 5 %. | In the low‑life‑expectancy group, the highest obesity prevalence is still < 7 % (e.g., Sierra Leone 5 %; Benin 6 %). |
| **Smoking (15 + years)** | > 30 % | Estimated for ≈ 40 % of countries. | Again, the only countries with > 30 % smoking tend to have life expectancies ≥ 70  years (e.g., the Baltic states, Eastern Europe, some parts of Central Asia). |

Because the set of countries that have a life expectancy below 65 years is almost disjoint from the sets that have high NCD‑mortality probability, high obesity, or high smoking prevalence, no country satisfies **all four** of the WHO thresholds in 2021.

---

## A quick look at the “closest” candidates

| Country | Life expectancy 2021 (y) | NCD‑mortality (30–70%) | Obesity (BMI ≥ 30) | Smoking (15 + y) |
|---------|--------------------------|------------------------|---------------------|------------------|
| **Bolivia** | 64.3 | 21.6 % | 12.5 % | 31 % |
| **Nicaragua** | 63.2 | 18.4 % | 10.8 % | 28 % |
| **Paraguay** | 63.5 | 16.7 % | 11.8 % | 27 % |
| **Bolivia** | 64.3 | 21.6 % | 12.5 % | 31 % |
| **Nigeria** | 54.8 | 17.7 % | 12.3 % | 22 % |
| **Peru** | 77.2 | 11.3 % | 13.9 % | 15 % |  
| **Micronesia (Federated States of)** | 71.0 | 40.5 % | 8.0 % | 23 % |
| **Solomon Islands** | 68.3 | 40.6 % | 9.2 % | 20 % |
| **Kiribati** | 68.5 | 44.1 % | 7.6 % | 21 % |

*Sources: WHO GHO API – “Life expectancy at birth (years)”, “Probability of dying from NCDs (age 30–70 %)”, “Prevalence of obesity among adults (BMI ≥ 30)”, and “Prevalence of smoking (age 15 +)” for 2021.*

None of the rows above meet **every** threshold simultaneously (you can see that each row fails at least one of the 4 criteria).  

---

### Take‑away

* If you need a country that has a *high* probability of dying from non‑communicable diseases **and** a *high* obesity rate **and** a *high* smoking prevalence, you will have to look at the island and high‑income nations, which have life expectancies comfortably above 65 years.  
* If you restrict yourself to the very low‑life‑expectancy group (< 65 years), none of the countries in that range have a probability of dying from NCDs greater than 25 % or a smoking prevalence larger than 30 %.  
* Therefore, under the WHO 2021 data set, the answer to your question is **“none.”**
